generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the broadleaf program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Abrams and Ferris's Illustrated Flora of the Pacific States, volume 4 (1960), read in full: corolla campanulate, funnelform or tubular, 5-lobed and commonly two-lipped; anther-bearing stamens 2 or 4 on the corolla tube; ovary mostly 2-celled. Plants of the World Online (as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read): flowers hypogynous, ovary superior; the fifth stamen usually a staminode.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 239 Bignoniaceae: trees or shrubs, sometimes climbing, very rarely herbs; leaves opposite, rarely alternate, mostly compound; stipules absent; fruit a capsule, or fleshy and not opening.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 239 Bignoniaceae: trees or shrubs, sometimes climbing, very rarely herbs; leaves opposite, rarely alternate, mostly compound; stipules absent; fruit a capsule, or fleshy and not opening. The books add whorled (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 414: opposite, sometimes whorled.

traits.leaf_division.note: Wikipedia Bignoniaceae (read 2026-10-17): about 810 to 860 species; leaves usually compound (two- or three-foliolate, pinnate or palmate), rarely simple. The liana tribe Bignonieae, the family's largest, carries the compound habit; simple leaves (Catalpa, Crescentia and kin) kept as sometimes so those genera stay drawable. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 414, family Bignoniaceae: inflorescence cyme, raceme or solitary, usually; read as {"cyme": "often", "raceme": "often", "solitary": "often"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 414, family Bignoniaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite; read as "hermaphrodite".
